title: Lipschitz continuity of Gaussian product density averages
statement: Let $I$ be a finite index set, let $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $|f(z)|\le1$ for every $z$, and let $v>0$. For mean vector $c$, integrate $f(z)$ times the mean derivative of the product Gaussian density with variance $v$ in each coordinate over Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^I$. As a function of $c$, this linear-functional-valued integral is Lipschitz with constant $2|I|^2/v$, using the maximum norm on mean vectors and the operator norm on linear functionals.
hypotheses_covered: $v$ is a nonzero nonnegative real, hence positive
replaced: Let $I$ be finite and $v\ge0$. Write $p_v(c,z)$ for the $N(c,v)$ density when $v>0$ and set $p_0(c,z)=0$; define $G_v(c,z)=\prod_{i\in I}p_v(c_i,z_i)$ and interpret division by zero as zero. Let $A_v(c,z)$ be the linear functional $h\mapsto\sum_i\bigl(\prod_{j\ne i}p_v(c_j,z_j)\bigr)((z_i-c_i)/v)p_v(c_i,z_i)h_i$. Let $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $|f|\le1$. If $v>0$, the map $c\mapsto\int f(z)A_v(c,z)\,dz$ is globally $2|I|^2/v$-Lipschitz, with maximum norm on mean vectors and operator norm on linear functionals.
